sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
sources.summary: Synthetic benchmark (13 tasks: retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation, QA) showing that models which ace vanilla NIAH still degrade sharply with length; of 17 models claiming 32K+ only about half held up at 32K. Established the 'effective context length' framing.
sources.popularity_signal: De-facto standard effective-context benchmark, reported in most 2024-2026 model cards; exact citation count unknown

sources.title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
sources.venue_or_author: Kelly Hong, Anton Troynikov, Jeff Huber (Chroma Research)
sources.summary: Tested 18 frontier models (Claude 4, GPT-4.1/o3, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3) with NIAH variants, LongMemEval and a repeated-words task; performance degrades with input length even far below the window, worse with low question-needle similarity and distractors. Argues for deliberate context engineering over 'just stuff the window'.
sources.popularity_signal: Coined the widely used term 'context rot'; heavily referenced in 2025-26 context-engineering writing (Hamel Husain, ZenML, Morph)

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.summary: Shows a U-shaped curve: models retrieve information best at the start or end of the context and markedly worse in the middle, even for explicitly long-context models. Foundational result behind 'put important context first/last' guidance.
sources.popularity_signal: Foundational; thousands of citations

sources.title: LongBench v2: Towards Deeper Understanding and Reasoning on Realistic Long-context Multitasks
sources.summary: 503 hard multiple-choice questions over contexts from 8K to 2M words across six task types (single/multi-doc QA, long ICL, dialogue history, code repos, structured data). Moves long-context evaluation from retrieval toward reasoning.
sources.popularity_signal: Successor to the widely used LongBench; ACL 2025 main track

sources.title: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation
sources.summary: Announces Llama 4 Scout with a claimed 10M-token context via the iRoPE architecture (interleaved attention layers without positional embeddings plus inference-time attention temperature scaling), trained at 256K. Long-context evidence given is NIAH retrieval and NLL over 10M tokens of code only.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor announcement; widely covered and widely criticised

sources.title: Llama 4 smells bad
sources.summary: Critique of the Llama 4 launch arguing the 10M context is nominal: Meta published only NIAH (no RULER/NoLiMa), and independent long-context tests such as Fiction.LiveBench showed steep degradation at far shorter lengths.
sources.popularity_signal: unknown; representative of the widespread community pushback

sources.title: 1M context is now generally available for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6
sources.summary: Anthropic makes the 1M-token window GA for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 (March 2026) at standard pricing with no long-context surcharge, positioning whole-codebase and multi-document requests as in-scope.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor announcement

sources.title: Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API
sources.summary: GPT-4.1 family (April 2025) ships a 1M-token context window in the API with improved long-context comprehension claims; ChatGPT remained capped at 32K, illustrating the API-vs-product gap in effective context.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor announcement

sources.title: Prompt caching - Claude Platform Docs
sources.summary: Explicit cache_control breakpoints (max 4) or automatic top-level caching; 5-min (1.25x write) or 1-hour (2x write) TTL, reads at 0.1x; cache hierarchy tools -> system -> messages, 20-block lookback, per-model minimum cacheable tokens (512-4096). Guidance: put static content first, mark the end of the stable prefix, never cache blocks containing changing content like timestamps, pre-warm with max_tokens=0.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor docs; pattern copied by Bedrock/Vertex and most gateways

sources.title: Prompt caching | OpenAI API
sources.summary: Automatic prefix caching for prompts >=1024 tokens in 128-token increments; cached input billed at 0.1x (cache writes free before GPT-5.6, 1.25x after). Retention 5-10 min in-memory up to 1h, extended retention up to 24h on newer models; prompt_cache_key steers routing (~15 rpm per key). Best practice: static instructions/tools/schemas first, variable content last; monitor cached_tokens.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor docs

sources.title: Context caching | Gemini API
sources.summary: Gemini offers implicit caching (on by default for 2.5+ models, discount passed through on prefix hits) and explicit CachedContent objects with a TTL that guarantee savings but add storage-time billing; cached tokens are billed at ~10% of input price.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor docs

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Models now support implicit caching
sources.summary: Announces implicit (automatic) caching for Gemini 2.5 so that requests sharing a common prefix receive the cached-token discount with no cache management; recommends placing repeated content at the start of the prompt to maximise hits.
sources.popularity_signal: Primary vendor announcement

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
sources.summary: Introduces PagedAttention, which stores KV cache in non-contiguous virtual-memory-style blocks, yielding near-zero KV memory waste and copy-on-write sharing across requests; vLLM built on it delivers 2-4x throughput over FasterTransformer/Orca at equal latency.
sources.popularity_signal: Foundation of vLLM, the most widely used open-source serving engine; thousands of citations

sources.title: Automatic Prefix Caching - vLLM design docs
sources.summary: Each KV block is keyed by hash(prefix tokens + block tokens) in a global table so identical prefixes share physical blocks; eviction removes zero-refcount blocks LRU-first (longest prefix as tiebreak), which is equivalent to RadixAttention's policy for full-attention models without an explicit tree.
sources.popularity_signal: Official docs of the dominant OSS serving engine

sources.title: Fast and Expressive LLM Inference with RadixAttention and SGLang
sources.summary: RadixAttention keeps the KV cache of all requests in a radix tree with LRU eviction, so multi-turn chats, few-shot prompts and tree-of-thought calls automatically reuse shared prefixes; reports large throughput gains on prefix-heavy workloads versus recomputation.
sources.popularity_signal: Origin of SGLang (major OSS serving engine); widely referenced

sources.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
sources.summary: Systems paper pairing RadixAttention prefix reuse with a compressed finite-state machine for faster constrained/structured decoding and API speculative execution, showing how structured-output constraints and KV reuse co-design reduce latency for agentic programs.
sources.popularity_signal: NeurIPS 2024; basis of SGLang

sources.title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
sources.summary: A KV cache layer that spills KV from GPU to CPU RAM, local disk and remote stores and shares it across vLLM/SGLang instances, so repeated long contexts are loaded rather than re-prefilled; reports multi-x TTFT/throughput gains on long-context, multi-turn and RAG workloads.
sources.popularity_signal: Default offload backend of vLLM production-stack; GitHub stars unknown

sources.title: production-stack tutorial 05: Offload KV cache
sources.summary: Hands-on guide to enabling LMCache in a vLLM Kubernetes deployment to offload KV cache to CPU or disk and to share it across pods via a remote cache server, raising hit rates beyond what GPU memory alone permits.
sources.popularity_signal: Official vLLM project docs

sources.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks (StreamingLLM)
sources.summary: Discovers that initial tokens act as 'attention sinks'; keeping their KV plus a sliding window of recent tokens lets models stream over millions of tokens with bounded memory and no fine-tuning, at the cost of forgetting evicted middle content.
sources.popularity_signal: Widely cited; popular GitHub repo (exact stars unknown)

sources.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
sources.summary: Keeps a small set of 'heavy hitter' tokens (high accumulated attention) plus recent tokens in the KV cache; with 20% heavy hitters it reports up to 29x throughput over HF Accelerate while preserving quality on OPT models.
sources.popularity_signal: Foundational KV eviction paper; widely cited

sources.title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
sources.summary: Uses an observation window at the end of the prompt to predict which prompt KV entries matter, then pools/clusters and keeps only those before decoding, compressing long-prompt KV with minimal accuracy loss.
sources.popularity_signal: Widely used baseline in KV-compression papers

sources.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
sources.summary: Quantizes keys per-channel and values per-token to 2 bits without fine-tuning, cutting peak memory 2.6x and enabling up to 4x batch size and 2.35-3.47x throughput on Llama-2, Falcon and Mistral with comparable quality.
sources.popularity_signal: ICML 2024; reference implementation for 2-bit KV quantization

sources.title: The Pitfalls of KV Cache Compression
sources.summary: Critical evaluation showing KV cache compression can silently degrade behaviour in ways aggregate benchmarks miss, particularly adherence to instructions in multi-instruction/system prompts; argues eviction policies must be evaluated on instruction-following, not just perplexity or NIAH.
sources.popularity_signal: unknown

sources.title: Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning
sources.summary: Evaluates KV-cache compression on long chain-of-thought reasoning models, where generated tokens dominate the cache; finds compression interacts with reasoning quality differently than on prompt-heavy tasks, informing whether eviction is safe for thinking-style workloads.
sources.popularity_signal: unknown

sources.title: Mistral 7B
sources.summary: Popularised sliding-window attention (each layer attends to the previous 4096 tokens, stacked layers give a longer effective span) with a rolling-buffer KV cache that bounds memory, plus grouped-query attention; ~2x speedup at 16K sequences.
sources.popularity_signal: Widely cited; basis of the Mistral open-weight line

sources.title: Gemma 3 Technical Report
sources.summary: Interleaves 5 local sliding-window (1024-token) attention layers per 1 global layer, cutting KV-cache memory overhead at 32K from ~60% to under 15% while supporting 128K context via RoPE rescaling.
sources.popularity_signal: Major open-weight release; widely referenced architecture pattern

sources.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
sources.summary: Selective state-space model with input-dependent dynamics that scales linearly in sequence length and carries a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing KV cache, matching Transformers on language modelling with ~5x higher inference throughput.
sources.popularity_signal: Thousands of citations; GitHub state-spaces/mamba widely used

sources.title: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
sources.summary: Interleaves attention and Mamba layers at a 1:7 ratio with MoE, giving a 256K context that fits on a single 80GB GPU with ~8x smaller KV cache than Mixtral; shows hybrids keep retrieval ability that pure SSMs lose.
sources.popularity_signal: ICLR 2025; AI21 Jamba 1.5/1.6 product line; reference hybrid design

sources.title: microsoft/LLMLingua (LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua-2)
sources.summary: Token-level prompt compression: a small LM (or a distilled token classifier in LLMLingua-2) drops low-information tokens for up to 20x compression; LongLLMLingua reorders and compresses long RAG contexts to counter lost-in-the-middle, reporting up to 21.4% RAG gains at a quarter of the tokens.
sources.popularity_signal: 6.6k GitHub stars

sources.title: Long-Context Inference at Scale: The Hidden Infrastructure Cost
sources.summary: Practitioner walkthrough of why long contexts are expensive: prefill attention is quadratic so TTFT stretches from ms to seconds, KV memory grows linearly per token and caps batch size, and per-request cost scales with total context even when most of it is static.
sources.popularity_signal: unknown
